MINUTES OF THE MORNING SESSION
THURSDAY, JUNE 20, 1940
Faunce House, Brown University
Providence, Rhode Island
BEFORE
the formal opening of the Convention, President Henry Merritt
Wriston of Brown University was presented by Dean Otis E. Randall,
Sigma '84, and officiaUy welcomed the Convention to Brown.
After Dr. Wriston withdrew, the Convention was called to order at
10:35 A.M., at Faunce House, Brown University, Providence, Rhode Island,
by Scott Turner, Phi '02, President of the Executive Council, who appointed
the following temporary officers :
Temporary President�
Carl Morton, Sigma '40
Temporary Recorder�
Matthew J. Mitchell, Sigma '42
Brother Morton welcomed the visiting Brothers on behalf of the
Sigma, and then appointed the following committees, disregarding the usual
rotation because a number of the Chapter delegates had not yet arrived:
On Credentials :
Robert C. Graham, Sigma '40, Chairman
George W. Fisher, Sigma '41
Samuel J. Sherer, II, Sig^ma '40
On Permanent Organization :
John J. Chester, Jr., Gamma '41, Chairman
Charles W. Pfeiffer, Omega '40
Albert E. Schmus, Omega '41
Motion was duly made, seconded and passed, that the Convention take
a recess to enable the Committees to prepare their reports.
At the end of the recess. Temporary President Carl Morton, Sigma '40,
called the Convention to order.
The Committee on Credentials reported that the following delegates
had presented their credentials, which were in order :

Scott Turner, Phi '02

LeRoy J. Weed, Theta '01
On motion duly made, seconded and passed, this report was accepted.
The Committee on Permanent Organization presented its report, making
the following nominations :
President Scott Turner, Phi '02
1st Vice-President Colonel H. Anthony Dyer, Sigma '94
2nd Vice-President Edward T. Richards, Sigma '27
3rd Vice-President Dean Otis E. Randall, Sigma '84
4th Vice-President Norman S. Dike, Sigma '85
5th Vice-President Benjamin T. Burton, Chi '21
6th Vice-President. .

7th Vice-President Dr. C. S. F. Lincoln, Kappa '91
Recorder Matthew J. Mitchell, Sigma '42
Assistant Recorder Joseph F. Lockett, Jr., Sigma '42
Assistant Recorder Charles M. Raymond, Sigma '42
On motion duly made, seconded and passed, this report was unanimously
accepted and the Temporary Recorder was instructed to cast one ballot for
the election of the permanent officers nominated. President Turner then
took the chair.
A message from Senator Theodore Francis Green, Sigma '87, was then
read to the Convention.
Brother Carl Morton, Sigma '40, then read the Convention Rules. These
were approved, and a motion made, seconded and passed that the rules as
read be accepted for this Convention.
The Annual Communication of the Executive Council was read by
LeRoy J. Weed, Theta '01, a member of the Executive Council.

On motion duly made, seconded and passed, this communication was
accepted, placed on file and referred to the Committee on Annual Com
munications.
President Turner then appointed the following Standing Committees :

On motion duly made, seconded and passed, it was voted to adjourn
the Convention untU Thursday, June 20, 1940, at 2:00 P. M.
MINUTES OF THE AFTERNOON SESSION
THURSDAY. JUNE 20, 1940
Faunce House, Brown University
Providence. Rhode Island
The meeting was called to order by President Turner at 2 :00 P. M.
Page Five

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
The minutes of the morning session were read, and on motion duly
made, seconded and passed, were approved.
Communications from Charles P. Spooner, Rho '94, and Howard Heydon, Sigma '05, were read.
On motion duly made, seconded and passed, it was voted to postpone
the reading of the Treasurer's Report.
Copies of the Table of Vital Statistics of the Fraternity for the year
ending March 1, 1940, were distributed.
Oral reports of the following Chapters were made by the delegates
present :
Delta Kappa Xi
Sigma Psi Upsilon
Gamma Iota
Lambda Omega
During the session, President Turner introduced the following mem
bers of the Executive Council and other alumni of the Fraternity, each of
whom spoke briefly: R. Bourke Corcoran, Omega '15; LeRoy J. Weed,
Theta '01; Frederick S. Fales, Gamma '96; Colonel H. Anthony Dyer,
Sigma '94; Maurice A. Wolf, Sigma '14; Dr. C. S. F. Lincoln, Kappa '91;
William M. Ingraham, Kappa '95 ; Judge Norman S. Dike, Sigma '85, and
Frederick Schwinn, Sigma '05.
On motion duly made, seconded and passed, it was voted to adjourn
the Convention, until 10:00 A. M., June 21. 1940.
MINUTES OF THE MORNING SESSION
FRIDAY, JUNE 21, 1940
Faunce House, Brown University
Providence, Rhode Island
The meeting was caUed to order by President Turner at 10:20 A. M.
The minutes of the previous afternoon session were read, and, on
motion duly made, seconded and passed, were approved.
The Committee on Credentials reported that the following delegates had
presented their credentials, which were in order :

Page Six

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
A discussion followed in regard to the desirability and feasibility of
establishing a Chapter of Psi Upsilon near the Epsilon.
The Committee to Nominate Members of the Executive CouncU pre
sented its report, nominating each of the following Brothers for membership
on the Executive Council for the usual term of five years :
Benjamin T. Burton, Chi '21
Edward T. Richards. Sigma '27
Alfred H. Morton. Omicron '19
Motion was duly made, seconded and passed that the report be unani
mously adopted and that the Recorder be instructed to cast a single ballot
electing each of the Brothers nominated to the Executive Council for the
usual term of five years.
On motion duly made, seconded and passed, it was voted that the Con
vention be adjourned untU 10:00 A. M., June 22, 1940.
MINUTES OF THE MORNING SESSION
SATURDAY, JUNE 22, 1940
Faunce House, Brown University
Providence. Rhode Island
The Convention was called to order by President Turner at 10 :10 A. M.
The minutes of the previous afternoon session were read, and on mo
tion duly made, seconded and passed, were approved.
Oral Chapter reports were given by the delegates of the following
Chapters :
Omicron Theta Theta Nu
Delta Delta Epsilon Phi
A greeting from Paul D. O'Brien, Sigma '27. was read.
The following members of the Executive Council and other alumni
Brothers were introduced and spoke briefly : Stephen G. Kent. Delta Delta
'11; AUen Northey Jones. Beta Beta '17; John C. Esty, Gamma '22; Royal
C. Taft. Sigma '85; Thomas L. Pierce. Kappa '98, and Peter A. GaBauer,
Pi '25.
Brother GaBauer, as Archivist of the Fraternity, reviewed the Chapter
histories received for the new
Epitome, and urged all Chapters which had
not already done so to finish their histories as soon as possible. He spoke
also of the excellent new archive arrangement instigated by President
Turner.
The report of the Committee on Annual Communications was read by
the Chairman, Park L. Brown, Omicron '41, making recommendations as
foUows :
I. That the Convention express its deep appreciation for the
cordial and generous hospitality extended by Brown University, its
Page Eight

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
President and Trustees, and by the Sigma Chapter, its undergradu
ates and alumni, and also for the efficient arrangements for our com
fort and enjoyment made by the Convention Committee of the Sigma.
2. That the Convention express its appreciation for the generous
services of time and effort contributed by the members of the Execu
tive Council exerted on behalf of the active Chapters of the Fra
ternity.
3. That the Recorder of the Convention write Brothers Oliver
D. Keep, Delta Delta '25, and John A. Cooper. Delta Delta '39, ex
pressing the appreciation of the Fraternity for their efficient and
loyal services in editing The Diamond.
4. That the Convention express its grateful acknowledgment and
appreciation of the real contribution of the Board of Governors of
the Alumni Association of Psi Upsilon in arousing interest and en
thusiasm on the part of the alumni of the Fraternity as a whole.
5. That the Recorder be directed to send telegrams of greeting to :
Earl D. Babst, Iota-Phi '93
Edward L. Stevens. Chi '99
Archibald Douglas. Lambda '94
Charles P. Spooner. Rho '94
6. That the following recommendations be referred to the Com
mittee on New Business :
A. That the Constitution be amended to include all past presi
dents and all future ex-presidents of the Executive CouncU as
members of the Executive Council with full voting rights. This .
recommendation contemplates the revision of Article II. Section
6. of the Constitution.
B. That this Convention recommend to the Executive CouncU
that Psi Upsilon become a member of the National Interfra
ternity Conference. Adoption of the following resolution was
proposed :
Resolved: That the Executive Council, in its discretion, be
and hereby is authorized to arrange for membership of Psi
Upsilon in the National Interfraternity Conference.
C. That the request of the Gamma Chapter to act as host to
the 1941 Convention be granted.
7. That the Convention express to Brother Peter A. GaBauer.
Pi '25, its deep appreciation for his unselfish labor in cataloguing the
valuable archives of the Fraternity.
8. That the Convention acknowledge the diligent and efficient
services of Brother A. Northey Jones, Beta Beta '17, as Treasurer
of the Fraternity.
Page Nine

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
9. That this Convention record its appreciation for the contribu
tions made to the Fraternity by R. Bourke Corcoran, Omega '15,
during the past twenty years. It was in May. 1920. that he was first
elected to the Executive Council. He has served continuously since
that time. For fifteen years he was Editor of The Diamond. He
served as news-gatherer, editor, and sole creator of its editorial pol
icy, without compensation of any kind except the fact that he was
performing a useful and necessary function on behalf of Psi Upsilon.
His unselfish devotion over the years has been as unswerving as his
faithful loyalty and self-effacement.
Upon motion duly made, seconded and passed, this report was accepted.
Upon motion duly made, seconded and passed, it was referred to the
Committee on New Business.
James T. Wolstenholme, Delta '40, presented the report of the Com
mittee on Unfinished Business. The sole recommendation urged all Chapter
delegates to see that their respective Chapter histories were being under
taken and finished.
President Turner heartily endorsed this recommendation.
The report of the Committee on New Business was read by John M.
Mitchell, Lambda '40. It recommended the adoption of the following reso
lutions :
1. Resolved: That the Recorder be directed to write an expres
sion of gratitude to President Wriston of Brown University for his
welcome to the Convention on behalf of the University.
2. Resolved: That this Convention hereby express to Brown
University its appreciation for its cordial hospitality and the generous
extension of the campus facilities for use by the convention delegates.
3. Resolved: That the Convention hereby express to Brother
H. Anthony Dyer, Sigma '94, its appreciation of his warm-hearted
invitation to Brown University and the Sigma Chapter; his words
were fulfilled in every respect.
4. Resolved: That the delegates and members of the Psi Upsilon
Fraternity assembled in Convention in its I07th year as guests of the
Sigma Chapter, Brown University, Providence, Rhode Island, on
June 20, 21, and 22, 1940, extend their gratitude to the Sigma Chapter,
its undergraduates and alumni, for their cordial reception of the del
egates and members attending the Convention.
5. Resolved: That the Convention appreciates the generous con
tribution of time and effort made by members of the Executive
CouncU in promoting the welfare of the active Chapters and the
entire Fraternity.
6. Resolved: That this Convention expresses to Brother R.
Bourke Corcoran, Omega '15, its profound appreciation for his faithPage Ten

RECORDS OF THE CONVENTION
ful services to the Fraternity as a member of the Executive Council
for the past twenty years, 1920-1940. His untiring efforts and effective
work for the welfare of the Fraternity stand as an example to all
Brothers.
7. Resolved: That the Convention hereby records its apprecia
tion of the unselfish and effective efforts of the officers and Board of
Governors of the Alumni Association of Psi Upsilon.
8. Resolved: That the delegates of this Convention convey to
Brothers Oliver D. Keep, Delta Delta '25, and John A. Cooper, Delta
Delta '39, their sincere gratitude for their outstanding accomplish
ments as Editor and Assistant Editor respectively of The Diamond.
9. Resolved: That the Recorder be directed to send telegrams of
greeting from the Convention to:
Earl D. Babst, Iota-Phi '93
Edward L. Stevens, Chi '99
Archibald Douglas, Lambda '94
Charles P. Spooner, Rho '94
10. Resolved: That the Executive CouncU in its discretion be,
and hereby is, authorized to arrange for membership of Psi Upsilon
in the National Interfraternity Conference.
11. Resolved: That in the event that two or more Chapters do
not subsequently object as provided in the Constitution, Section 6 of
Article II of the Constitution be, and it hereby is, amended to read
as follows :
"Article II, Section 6 : The Convention held in the year 1908
shall elect an Executive Council of ten. a majority of whom shall
be graduate members of the Fraternity and no more than two
from the same Chapter. The said Council, at its first meeting
after its election shall divide itself by lot into five classes of two
members each, whose respective terms of office shall be one, two,
three, four and five years. Thereafter, the Convention shall annu
ally elect two members to replace the outgoing class and to serve
for five years each.
"Commencing with the Convention held in April 1932, each
Convention shall elect, for a five year term, one additional mem
ber to the Executive CouncU, untU its membership shall have
been increased to fifteen, and thereafter three members shall be
elected annually to fill the vacancies caused by the expiration of
terms. In addition to the fifteen elected members of the Council,
all present and future ex-Presidents of the Executive Council
shall be life members of the Executive Council, with full voting
rights.
"The headquarters of the Council shall be in the City of
New York. The Council shall elect a President, a Secretary and
Page Eleven

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
Treasurer, shall regulate its own proceedings and assignments of
duty and shall be empowered to employ a member of the Fra
ternity to act as Assistant Secretary and who shall receive there
for such compensation as shall be authorized by the Convention.
The Council shall issue calls and make all arrangements for
special conventions when requested to do so, in writing, by at
least five Chapters ; shall give official announcements of the pass
age of any measure requiring the consent of the Chapters ; shall
keep the Fraternity seal, all Fraternity property, the official copy
of the Constitution and Convention records, a copy of the laws
of each Chapter and as complete statistics of them as possible.
It shall have power under the regulation of the Convention to
make and collect assessments on the several Chapters in propor
tion to the number of members in each ; shall allow claims against
the Fraternity ; shall superintend the publication of Fraternity
documents; shaU decide all points at issue between Chapters
when appealed to. The Council shall fill its own vacancies and
shall submit annually to the Convention a communication em
bracing a report of its transactions .with such recommendations as
to the affairs of the Fraternity as it may deem proper. The
Council may investigate applications for charters of the Frater
nity and. upon its own motion, may inquire into the expediency of
establishing a Chapter at any college or university. Within thirty
days after the close of any such investigation or inquiry, the
Council shall transmit to each Chapter or to the Convention its
finding of facts and recommendations. The Council shall, at regu
lar periods, cause the Chapters to be visited by one or more of
its members, the expense of such visitation to be met out of funds
to be specially contributed or otherwise provided for that pur
pose. The contents of any report on such visitation shall be
communicated only to the CouncU and to the members or alumni
of the Chapter visited."
12. Resolved: That this Convention accept the invitation of the
Gamma Chapter to hold the 1941 Convention with this Chapter in
celebration of the centennial of its establishment at Amherst.
Upon motion duly made, seconded and passed, the report of the Com
mittee on New Business was accepted, and all resolutions proposed by such
Committee, with the exception of Resolution No. 10. were adopted.
A discussion followed in regard to the advantages and disadvantages of
joining the National Interfraternity Conference, the delegates of the Omega
and Epsilon Phi Chapters opposing this step. After considerable debate,
upon motion duly made, seconded and passed. Resolution No. 10 proposed
by the Committee on New Business was adopted.
Upon motion duly made, seconded and passed, the Convention took a
recess until immediately after the conclusion of the ceremony of presentaPage Twelve

RECORDS OF THE CONVENTION
tion of a Memorial Gate to Brown University by the Sigma Chapter in
commemoration of its one hundred years of existence at that University.
President Turner again called the Convention to order at 12:55 P. M.
Upon motion duly made, seconded and passed, a vote of thanks was
extended to the Convention officers.
Upon motion duly made, seconded and passed, it was voted that the
Convention be adjourned sine die.
There being no further business. President Scott Turner declared the
Convention adjourned sine die.
Respectfully submitted,
Matthew J. Mitchell,
Sigma 42, Recorder.
RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED

its discretion be, and it hereby is, authorized to arrange for membership of

General Resolution No. 2, Resolved: That this Convention accept the
invitation of the Gamma Chapter to hold the 1941 Convention with this
Chapter in celebration of the centennial of its establishment at Amherst.
General Resolution No. 3. Resolved: That each of the following
alumni brothers be elected to the Executive Council for the usual term
of five years :
Benjamin T. Burton, Chi '21
Edward T. Richards, Sigma '27
Alfred H. Morton, Omicron '19

Special Resolution No. 1. Resolved: That the Recorder be directed
to write an expression of gratitude to President Wriston of Brown Univer
sity for his welcome to the Convention on behalf of the University.

Special Resolution No. 3. Resolved: That the Convention hereby ex

THE ANNUAL COMMUNICATION
OF THE
EXECUTIVE COUNCIL
TO THE
1940 CONVENTION OF PSI UPSILON
HELD UNDER THE AUSPICES OF THE
EXECUTIVE COUNCIL AND THE SIGMA CHAPTER
Providence, Rhode Island
June 20. 21 and 22, 1940
The Executive Council heartily welcomes the delegates of our twentyseven Chapters to this Convention held in the one hundred and seventh year
of our Fraternity.
All members of Psi Upsilon join with us in congratulating our hospi
table host, the Sigma Chapter, upon having attained its one hundredth birth
day, but most of all upon a record of outstanding achievement throughout
the past one hundred years of which the Sigma and all members of the
Fraternity may indeed be proud.
We are deeply grateful to the undergraduates, alumni and Convention
Committees of the Sigma for the generous arrangements announced for our
entertainment, and for the thoughtful attention given to each detail likely
to promote the success of this Convention.
We are likewise greatly indebted to Brown University, to its President,
Dr. Henry M. Wriston, and to its Board of Trustees, for the gracious
hospitality shown to us and for making available to our delegates its build
ings and facilities.
Chapter Visits :
Since our last Convention, in addition to several unofficial vishs, the
following seven official visits have been made by members of the Executive
Council :
Epsilon Henry N. Woolman
Iota Henry N. Woolman
Phi Benjamin T. Burton
Xi Edward T. Richards
Omicron R. Bourke Corcoran
Upsilon R. K. Northey
Chi Walter T. Collins
Page Seventeen

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
In addition, pursuant to General Resolution No. 3 of the Convention of
1939, under appointment by the Executive Council, Brother Gordon B.
McLaren, Nu '13, made an official visit to the Zeta Zeta Chapter.
The Condition of the Fraternity :
In general our chapters continue to be capably managed. Their business
affairs are well conducted. Alumni cooperation is welcomed and cheerfully
given by graduates of ability. The usual high quality of our undergraduate
membership is being maintained. Moreover, Psi Upsilon continues to fulfill a
useful place in the educational system and to build lasting loyalty in its
members by developing in them a conscientious approach to the tasks of the
college curriculum, higher qualities of character and manhood, and increased
capacity for sincere and loyal friendship�
all of which should lead to greater
happiness and higher attainments in later life. For a number of years, better
chapter administration has been promoted and interchapter friendships stim
ulated by annual informal conferences held by various chapter-groups. At
these conferences numerous chapter-problems have been discussed and the
favorable experience of one chapter has been available to others.
Unfortunately, however, during the last year scholastic records have
in a number of our chapters not measured up to the general intelligence of
their membership. Reports of scholastic standings of various fraternities
have been received from a number of colleges and universities. Certain of
our chapters are still doing outstandingly well. Nevertheless, entirely too
many of our chapters rank near the foot of the scholastic list. In some
cases this problem is already being aggressively attacked both by under
graduates and by alumni and steady progress is being achieved. We urge
upon all chapters constant attention to conscientious efforts to improve
scholastic rating.
The Alumni Association of Psi Upsilon :
During the past year the officers and Board of Governors of the Alumni
Association of Psi Upsilon have unselfishly given of their time and efforts
to further the interests of the Fraternity. In many ways the Association
has usefully supplemented the efforts of the Executive Council.
The annual meeting of the Alumni Association will take place at
3 :30 P. M., June 21, 1940, at the Sigma Chapter House and it is urged that
as many as possible of the alumni present, as well as members of the Class
of 1940, attend.
Petitions :
The Executive Council has no petition for a charter to submit to the
Convention. Nevertheless, attention is called to the fact that an active and
large group of alumni in southern California have expressed keen interest

RECORDS OF THE CONVENTION
in the establishment of a separate chapter of the Fraternity at the Univer
sity of California at Los Angeles. No specific group at that university
however, has as yet received their backing.
The Constitution :
After some unexpected delays the reprint of the Constitution of the
Fraternity with all amendments to date, which was mentioned in last year's
communication from the Executive Council, was
completed, and all the
members of the Council certified as to its authenticity. Distribution will be
held up until our chapters reassemble in the autumn. It is expected that
these new volumes will greatly assist chapter officers in following consti
tutional requirements.
_ _
One further amendment to the Constitution seems desirable. There are
living three former Presidents of the Executive Council�Earl D. Babst
Iota '93. Archibald Douglas. Lambda '94, and Edward L. Stevens. Chi '99'
Service as president of the Council of necessity creates an intimate knowl
edge of Psi Upsilon's affairs and gives a broad experience in meeting a
multitude of fraternity problems. In order that all ex-presidents of the
Executive Council may be encouraged to attend Council meetings, and their
knowledge and experience may be more
readily available, the Executive
Council recommends that Article II. Section 6. of the Constitution be
amended so that in addition to the fifteen elected members of the Executive
Council all present and future ex-presidents of the Executive Council shall
be life members of the Council, with full voting rights.
The Diamond:
Brother Oliver D. Keep, Deha Delta '25. a member of the Advisory
Committee on The Diamond and an experienced publisher, unselfishly volun
teered to serve this year as Acting Editor of The Diamond, and John A.
Cooper, Delta Delta '39, has served as Assistant Editor.
During the year much study was devoted to the form, set-up and con
tents of The Diamond with the object of giving to the Fraternity as wellpublished a magazine with the most interesting contents as the funds avail
able for publication make possible. The result has been a magazine which
reflects much credit on Psi Upsilon. Brothers Keep and Cooper have devoted
many hours to this effort and deserve the hearty thanks of the entire
Fraternity.
The Archives :
Since the last Convention the many valuable and interesting papers and
documents which go to make up the archives of the Executive Council, and
which cover the greater period of the Fraternity's existence, have been
removed from storage in Brooklyn and neatly assembled in a
modernlyPage Nineteen

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
equipped archives room adjoining the office of the Executive Council in
New York City. Moreover, a methodical index of these documents has been
prepared and is being maintained
Practically all the labor involved in accomplishing this effort has been
contributed by our indefatigable archivist, Peter A. GaBauer, Pi '25.
Acknowledgment, however, should be made of personal gifts from Earl D.
Babst, Iota '93, and Walter T. Collins, Iota '03, which, added to funds allo
cated by the Executive Council, made possible this result.
Finding that there were on hand more copies of old editions of cata
logues of the Fraternity than the Executive Council required, extra copies
of all such catalogues on hand were distributed to libraries of various col
leges and universities and other reference libraries desiring to receive them.
In this way insurance has been obtained for the preservation of the records
of our Fraternity in future years.
The Second Epitome:
An active working committee of prominent alumni have made real
progress in compiling the material for our second epitome. Real cooperation
is now being obtained from chapters which have not heretofore prepared
and sent in their histories. There is, therefore, promise that this task may
be completed within the near future.
The National Interfraternity Conference:
For many years Psi Upsilon has not been a member of the National
Interfraternity Conference, although during the last few years the Confer
ence has voluntarily supplied to the Executive Council a great deal of the
information and material distributed to its members. Much of this is of a
character that is distinctly helpful.
The taking out of membership by Psi Upsilon in the National Interfra
ternity Conference has received considerable study. Although at first hesi
tant, after carefully weighing the subject, the Executive Council has con
cluded that it would be to the advantage of Psi Upsilon to become a member
of the Conference provided Alpha Delta Phi also joins the Conference and
Delta Kappa Epsilon continues to maintain its membership. The Executive
Council, therefore, urges this Convention to go on record as favoring such
action.
In joining the National Interfraternity Conference Psi Upsilon retains
its independence of decision in managing its own affairs. The Conference
is merely advisory in character. The cost of membership is only |50 per year.
The coming years are likely to bring many problems to college frater
nities. The National Interfraternity Conference provides a medium through
which on behalf of all fraternities these problems may be discussed with
college authorities and the fraternity viewpoint presented. The absence
from membership of such fraternities as Psi Upsilon and Alpha Delta Phi
Page Twenty

PSI UPSILON FRATERNITY
is reported to have proved a distinct handicap to the officers of the National
Interfraternity Conference in efforts intended to benefit all fraternities.
As a long range proposition it is believed wise to work with the other
fraternities and to have a voice in shaping policies and activities which may
well affect our own future. For the information of the delegates, the Execu
tive Council of Alpha Delta Phi has arrived at a similar conclusion .
The Executive Council:
With this Convention the terms of Brothers Benjamin T. Burton, Ed
ward T. Richards and R. Bourke Corcoran expire. It is, therefore, encum
bent upon the Convention to elect to the Executive Council three brothers
for the usual terms of five years each.
During the year, the Executive Council has elected to its membership
to serve out the balance of the term of Cadwallader Evans, Jr., Eta '01,
which expires with the Convention of 1942, Herbert Judson Flagg, Theta
Theta '12. Brother Flagg was one of the charter members of the Theta
Theta and his interest in the chapter and in Psi Upsilon has continued
through the years following his graduation. We are indeed glad to have
him among our number and thus to increase representation on the Council
of our West-Coast chapters.
It is with deep sorrow that the Executive Council reports to the Con
vention the death on March 18, 1940, of Brother Henry Hill Pierce, Kappa
'96. Brother Pierce served as a member of the Council from November
1933 to December 1938, at which time he resigned. Before his election to
the Council Brother Pierce had brought distinction to Psi Upsilon by his
outstanding professional and business achievements which in and of them
selves testify to the high order of his abilities, the charm of his personality
and that fineness of character which brings respect from fellow men. In his
years of service on the Council he earned the affection and admiration of
his fellow members.
1941 Convention :
It is encumbent upon this Convention to fix the meeting place of the
1941 Convention. Unless otherwise determined, pursuant to Article II, Sec
tion 2. of the Constitution, it would become the privilege in regular rotation
of the Lambda Chapter to act as host.
We call your attention, however, to the fact that the Gamma Chapter,
which next year celebrates its centennial, has requested that the 1941 Con
vention be held with it, and that the Convention of 1939 recommended to
this Convention that the Gamma's request be granted. The Executive Coun
cil joins in this recommendation.
General :
We are living in days of sweeping world events, the ultimate effect of
which stagger one's imagination. Ideals of human conduct, of life and of
Page Twenty-one

RECORDS OF THE CONVENTION
religion which we hold dear are being challenged, and we are being scoffed
at for holding them. It is in such times that organizations like Psi Upsilon,
which seek to foster human fineness, can attain their greatest usefulness.
We urge our undergraduate brothers to maintain cool, clear thinking heads
and resolute hearts and to concentrate on doing well their daily tasks in
preparation for that which the future may hold in store. Whatever that
may be, we are confident that our brothers have the ability and the courage
to play their part as men and gentlemen, and that since no nation can long
control the modern world by force, days will again dawn when relationships
between men and nations will be governed by the spirit of peace and good
will.
Respectfully submitted.
The Committee of the Executive Council of Psi Upsilon

Report of the Treasurer
1940
There is presented herewith a comparative statement of the net worth
of the various funds of the Fraternity held by the Executive Council as of
April 30, 1939 and 1940. A list of investments held in the General Fund,
the Bridgman Fund and the Diamond Life Subscription Fund, showing the
cost and market value, is also presented.
It is to be noted that a new fund has been created this year, namely
the Diamond Life Subscription Fund. Into this have been paid all the $15
Diamond life subscriptions. The money has not been spent in defraying
Diamond expenses as was the case heretofore in respect of the $10 Diamond
life subscriptions, but has been placed in a reserve fund to be used only on
an annuity basis to provide for the costs of the life subscriptions for the
brothers who have paid the $15 life subscriptions. This is a sound policy,
and a great improvement over the previous unsound practice of disbursing
the life subscription funds in payment of present-day costs. The difficulty
with the new method is that we will be hard pushed to meet our current
printing and other Diamond costs. Thus in the current Diamond Fund there
was a deficit of $2,528.65 in the past fiscal year, offset to the extent of
$1,200 by transfers of $1,000 from the Bridgman Fund and $200 from the
General Fund. Until the annuities derived from the Diamond Life Subscrip
tion Fund reach substantial proportions it will be necessary to draw from
the General Fund and the Bridgman Fund each year to meet the current
Diamond expenses.
The cash position of the Fraternity continues favorable. All accounts
receivable were collected between April 30, 1940 and June 15, 1940. The un
realized loss on investments held in the three investment funds as of April
30, 1940 was $9,368.87, in comparison with $11,006.47 the previous year. This
bad situation has existed for a number of years, and while it would have
been possible to write down the value of the securities to market and take
the loss on the books, such action has not been taken but rather investments
have been made with a view to a possible eventual elimination of this loss.
If investments were carried in the statement at market value instead of at
cost, the aggregate net worth of the funds of the Fraternity would work
out as $35,174.20 as of April 30, 1940.
